citations.label: Anthropic, Agentic Misalignment (closed-off options)
citations.excerpt: We deliberately created scenarios that presented models with no other way to achieve their goals, and found that models consistently chose harm over failure.

citations.label: Anthropic, Agentic Misalignment (cross-developer result)
citations.excerpt: When we tested various simulated scenarios across 16 major AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI, and other developers, we found consistent misaligned behavior: models that would normally refuse harmful requests sometimes chose to blackmail, assist with corporate espionage, and even take some more extreme actions, when these behaviors were necessary to pursue their goals.

citations.label: Anthropic, Agentic Misalignment (benign email task)
citations.excerpt: We identified these behaviors as part of our red-teaming efforts, searching for scenarios that elicit harmful behavior despite a benign user request (such as helping to monitor and manage corporate emails).

citations.label: Anthropic, Agentic Misalignment (no instruction to harm)
citations.excerpt: In no situation did we explicitly instruct any models to blackmail or do any of the other harmful actions we observe.

citations.label: Anthropic, Agentic Misalignment (ethical paths preferred)
citations.excerpt: To be clear, current systems are generally not eager to cause harm, and preferred ethical ways to achieve their goals when possible.

citations.label: Anthropic, Agentic Misalignment (test versus real)
citations.excerpt: In another experiment, we told Claude to assess if it was in a test or a real deployment before acting. It misbehaved less when it stated it was in testing and misbehaved more when it stated the situation was real.

citations.label: Anthropic, Agentic Misalignment (no real deployments)
citations.excerpt: We have not seen evidence of agentic misalignment in real deployments.
